content.text:
The drawing shows two benzene rings joined by an NH bridge, each ring carrying a carboxylic acid.

**Left ring:** A benzene ring with a COOH group on the bottom carbon. The adjacent carbon (upper right) carries the NH, so the acid and the amine are ortho to each other.

**Right ring:** Its vertices, going around, are:
- C1, bottom, bearing COOH (at about 923, 825)
- C2, lower left, bearing NH (at about 836, 775)
- C3, upper left (at about 836, 675)
- C4, top, bearing Cl (at about 923, 625)
- C5, upper right (at about 1010, 675)
- C6, lower right (at about 1010, 775)

The COOH is on C1 and the NH is on C2, so they are ortho. The Cl on C4 is para to C1, the carbon carrying the COOH.

**SMILES:** Starting from the left-ring acid and going through the NH to the right ring:
OC(=O)c1ccccc1Nc1cc(Cl)ccc1C(=O)O

Checking the right ring in this string: c1 (bearing N), then c (C3), then c(Cl) (C4), then c (C5), c (C6), and c1 (C1, bearing the COOH). This matches the drawing, with Cl para to the COOH carbon and meta to the NH carbon.

SMILES: OC(=O)c1ccccc1Nc1cc(Cl)ccc1C(=O)O
